citation: S. Boucheron, G. Lugosi, P. Massart, On concentration of self-bounding functions, Electronic Journal of Probability 14 (2009), 1884-1899
exact_locator_and_range: Definition 2, printed pp. 1885-1886/text lines 108-117; coordinate-deletion notation and measurable surrogate, printed p. 1885/text lines 79 and 94-103; Theorem 1 independent-input and upper-tail clauses, printed pp. 1886-1887/text lines 160-183
hypotheses_and_range: independent inputs; nonnegative measurable finite-mean f; for every coordinate r a measurable f_r of x with coordinate r dropped; Definition 2 uses a,b>0 and requires 0<=f-f_r<=1 with sum_r(f-f_r)<=a*f+b; Theorem 1 states parameters a,b>=0 and an upper tail for every t>0
T187_parameter_substitution: Inputs are L=N+m-1 iid uniform decimal digits; F=(E_m(N)-N)/2; proposed fractional charge d_r=sum_{i<j} 1[B_i=B_j] 1[r in S_ij]/|S_ij|; after any scale C>0 the proposed functions are f=F/C and f_r=(F-d_r)/C. If measurability and the unit-drop bound held then sum_r(f-f_r)=f<=f+b for a=1 and every b>0.
precise_obstruction: For every N>=2 and m>=1, the unscaled proposed surrogate at coordinate zero depends on X_0 after all other digits are fixed: at all-zero digits it equals binom(N,2)-sum_{j=1}^{N-1}1/(m+min(j,m)), while after changing only X_0 it is at most binom(N-1,2). Their difference is at least (N-1)-sum_{j=1}^{N-1}1/(m+min(j,m))>=(N-1)/2>0. Thus Definition 2's dropped-coordinate domain/measurability hypothesis fails; nonzero scaling cannot repair it.
